A_henry_and_solubility.reading: Lange 0 C and 4 C values are used as primary. The compilation van 't Hoff with 2400 K is about 6-8 percent lower at 0 and 4 C. The Lange-implied slope between 0 and 25 C is about 2700 K, so the constant-slope form is an approximation.

assumptions.text: Soda specific heat equal to water (4.184 J/g K)
Ideal-gas molar volume at 0 C, 1 atm (22.414 L/mol); CO2 molar mass 44.01 g/mol
Henry's law linear from 1 atm to the pressure needed for 3.5 volumes at 4 C
CO2 partition ratio k_ice = 0 in base case (team premise; no sourced ice solubility number found)
Unfrozen pocket fraction and pocket CO2 retention: 0 in base case; sensitivity values not sourced
Cube size 25 g; 0.92 g/cm3 ice; cube geometry
Cube start -18 C (freezer); sensitivity case 0 C
Heat transfer coefficient h = 300 W/(m2 K) base; sweep 100 and 900
Cube surface area scales as (mass)^(2/3) during melt; constant-area variant also reported
Lumped liquid, adiabatic container, full immersion, no ambient heat gain
Pour-over water at 4 C and 3.5 vol; total serving 330 ml; melt water counted in total volume
Cube CO2 content zero for pour-over (team premise: CO2 lost on freezing)
CO2 is not modelled during the melt step; degassing during mixing is not modelled
Saturation at intermediate temperatures by linear interpolation between Lange points
Melt step runs in a 250 ml soda at 25 C with a 25 g cube (team computed task)
Heat of fusion 334.7 J/g; ice 2.05 J/g K; water 4.184 J/g K

open_items: Ice-phase CO2 segregation coefficient at atmospheric pressure: no sourced number found (k_ice = 0 is a premise).
Natural-convection h for a cube in still soda: only a search snippet (Waterloo 60-900) is available.
Solubility in ice: Dye-3 ice-core work says earlier lab CO2-in-ice values were too high; the new value is not given in the read text.
Pour-over at 4 C does not fully melt 2 cubes; the drink ends at 0 C with residual ice in the base case.
CO2 at pour-over and open-glass equilibrium with air (about 0.04 percent CO2) is not sourced in this run.
